title: Siramesine induced cell death of glioblastoma through inactivating the STAT3-MGMT signaling pathway.
authors: Cui, Xiaohang; Yao, Anhui; Lv, Jinquan; Zhang, Chi; Chen, Yue; Mei, Tingjie; Li, Hengzeng; Wu, Yahui; Jia, Liyun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Siramesine通过STAT3-MGMT信号通路诱导胶质母细胞瘤死亡，属于肿瘤药理学与信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM), the most prevalent invasive primary brain tumor in adults, is characterized by high mortality, frequent recurrence, and short survival time. The effectiveness of temozolomide (TMZ) in treating GBM is compromised by chemoresistance. Elevated levels of O6-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) and the activation of signal transduction and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) have been associated with GBM's resistance to TMZ chemotherapy. Although siramesine (Sira) has demonstrated antitumor activity in various cancers, its potential therapeutic effect in gliomas remains uncertain. METHODS: Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), healing assay, and clone formation assay were utilized to assess the cell viability, proliferation, and migration of glioma cells. RNAseq, molecular docking analysis, pull-down assay, qPCR, and pharmacologic treatment were employed to explore the cell signaling pathway. Tumor growth and STAT3 signaling pathway proteins in U87-MG cell-derived xenografts from nude mice were examined using Western blot. RESULTS: Our study demonstrated that Sira reduces cell viability, inhibits proliferation and migration, and induces autophagy in GBM cells. Sira promotes GBM cell death by binding to STAT3 and inhibiting phosphorylation of STAT3(Y705). Combination therapy of TMZ and Sira synergistically induced cell death and inhibited GBM cell proliferation and migration, potentially linked to decreased p-STAT3(Y705) and MGMT levels. Furthermore, using STAT3 signaling activators and inhibitors, we confirmed that reduced MGMT levels were mediated by STAT3 inactivation. Cell-derived xenografts from nude mice revealed that Sira did not affect glioma growth. However, it did inhibit the JAK2-STAT3-MGMT signaling pathway and decrease glioma stem cell properties. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that Sira inhibits the STAT3-MGMT signaling pathway, slowing tumor growth and increasing sensitivity to TMZ in GBM. These results lay a solid foundation for developing new GBM therapies, with Sira holding promise as a candidate for combined TMZ chemotherapy in GBM.
abstract_zh: 背景：胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）是成人中最常见的侵袭性原发脑肿瘤，以高死亡率、频繁复发和短生存期为特征。替莫唑胺（TMZ）治疗GBM的效果受到化疗耐药性的损害。O6-甲基鸟嘌呤DNA甲基转移酶（MGMT）水平升高及信号转导与转录激活因子3（STAT3）的激活与GBM对TMZ化疗的耐药性相关。尽管西拉美辛（Sira）已在多种癌症中显示出抗肿瘤活性，但其在胶质瘤中的潜在治疗效果仍不确定。方法：采用细胞计数试剂盒-8（CCK-8）、愈合实验和克隆形成实验评估胶质瘤细胞的活力、增殖和迁移。利用RNA测序、分子对接分析、pull-down实验、qPCR和药理学处理探索细胞信号通路。通过Western blot检测裸鼠U87-MG细胞来源异种移植瘤中的肿瘤生长和STAT3信号通路蛋白。结果：我们的研究表明，Sira降低GBM细胞的活力，抑制增殖和迁移，并诱导自噬。Sira通过结合STAT3并抑制STAT3（Y705）磷酸化促进GBM细胞死亡。TMZ和Sira的联合治疗协同诱导细胞死亡并抑制GBM细胞增殖和迁移，这可能与p-STAT3（Y705）和MGMT水平降低有关。此外，使用STAT3信号激活剂和抑制剂，我们确认MGMT水平降低是由STAT3失活介导的。裸鼠细胞来源异种移植瘤显示，Sira不影响胶质瘤生长。然而，它确实抑制了JAK2-STAT3-MGMT信号通路并降低了胶质瘤干细胞特性。结论：我们的发现表明，Sira抑制STAT3-MGMT信号通路，减缓肿瘤生长并增加GBM对TMZ的敏感性。这些结果为开发新的GBM疗法奠定了坚实基础，Sira有望成为GBM联合TMZ化疗的候选药物。
